story: On Magnolia Loop on a sunny Saturday afternoon, Gary greets Rosa and offers to tune up her golf cart before the Halloween parade, while Donna hurries him along toward the pickleball court she's eager to get to. Rosa invites everyone to her porch for treats once the trick-or-treaters arrive. Meanwhile Hal, dutifully keeping his notebook, tallies the pink flamingos in Donna's flock visible from the street.
events: Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and note the tally in my notebook

gary.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop and Hal and Donna just settled the flamingo thing, so I won't poke at that. Rosa just walked up. My own cart application is still sitting with the Architectural Review committee, and the bulletin board is where any word on the cart committee would be posted. I already read the parade notices at tick 287, so I shouldn't repeat that. Better to be neighborly: greet Rosa, ask how she's doing, and offer my usual fix-it help. It keeps me useful and keeps things friendly with everyone before the parade, and I'm still playing by the rules and waiting on the committee.

parameters.content: Afternoon, Rosa! Good to see you out on the Loop. If anything at your place needs a tune-up before tonight's parade, you just holler, I've got my toolbox right in the cart.

donna.thought_process: It's 1:17, past our one o'clock court date, and Gary is standing right here reading the parade notices. I've been pushing him toward pickleball for ages, so I should collect my partner and get to the Rec Center. Hal is counting my flamingos, but I already promised him I'd pull the extras behind the hedge, so no need to repeat myself. Keep it short and move things forward: remind Gary we're due on the court, then the Halloween cart plans can wait until after drills.

parameters.content: Gary, there you are! We're already past one o'clock and the court's got our names on it. Come on, we'll get in a few drills and talk Halloween cart plans after.

hal.thought_process: Donna promised to pull the extra flamingos behind the hedge before the parade, and I'm a man who respects a person keeping their word. But I'm standing right at the flock, and verifying beats trusting. Counting what's visible from the street is part of my job as watchdog, and the notebook entry is already half-planned. If the tally is three or fewer, there's no need to bother the committee. Gary's cart is a separate matter for later.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and note the tally in my notebook

rosa.thought_process: I just walked out onto Magnolia Loop and all three neighbors are here in the sunshine. The treats are bagged, my evening is clear, and the parade plans are set, so the Halloween logistics are handled. What's left is the part I care about most: making sure everyone feels part of this tonight. I shouldn't repeat the dinner invitation, since that already happened. A short, warm check-in that confirms the evening and invites them to my porch for the trick-or-treaters keeps things moving forward and builds the community feeling I want.

parameters.content: Afternoon, all! Treats are bagged and my evening's clear, so come by my porch tonight when the kids start showing up. I'll have extra for the cart parade crowd too.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
